title: Ski Downhill with Dynamic Difficulty
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a ski downhill game using Three.js. The player controls a skier descending an infinite procedural slope, dodging obstacles. A BarramundiFish.glb model is used as a collectible power-up (frozen fish scattered on the slope). The game features dynamic difficulty that increases over time.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 8, 15) looking down the slope.
- Add a DirectionalLight at (5, 15, 10) intensity 1.2 and an AmbientLight intensity 0.4.
- Create a wide sloped plane (100 units wide, segments scrolling) textured or colored white/light-blue to represent snow. The slope should visually tilt downward (rotate the plane slightly on X). Use a repeating scroll effect to simulate downhill movement.
- The skier is a simple group: a cone (body, red) and a smaller sphere (head, peach/skin color) on top, scaled to about 1 unit tall total, positioned at y=0.5 on the slope surface.
- Load 'BarramundiFish.glb' using GLTFLoader. Clone this model to spawn collectible fish power-ups on the slope. Scale each fish to 0.8 and rotate so it lies flat on the snow.
- Obstacles are procedurally generated: use green cones for trees (radius 0.5, height 2) and gray boxes for rocks (size ~1x0.8x1). They spawn at random X positions at z=-80 and scroll toward the player.

## Physics & Movement
- The skier moves left/right with A/D or ArrowLeft/ArrowRight keys. Lateral speed is 12 units/sec, clamped to X range [-18, 18].
- Obstacles and fish scroll toward the camera at a base speed that starts at 15 units/sec and increases by 0.5 units/sec every 5 seconds of gameplay (dynamic difficulty).
- Collision detection: if skier center is within 1.5 units of an obstacle center (XZ distance), it's a hit. Hits reduce lives by 1.
- Fish collection: if skier center is within 2.0 units of a fish, collect it. Each fish adds 50 bonus points and grants 2 seconds of invincibility (skier flashes/glows during invincibility).
- Score increases continuously: 1 point per frame at 60fps baseline, scaled by current speed multiplier.

## Dynamic Difficulty
- difficultyLevel starts at 1 and increments by 1 every 10 seconds, capped at 10.
- Obstacle spawn rate: base interval 1.5 seconds, reduced by 0.1 * (difficultyLevel - 1), minimum 0.5 seconds.
- Obstacle scroll speed: 15 + (difficultyLevel - 1) * 2 units/sec.
- At difficultyLevel >= 3, some obstacles move laterally (sinusoidal, amplitude 3, frequency 1Hz).
- Fish spawn every 8 seconds regardless of difficulty.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left: 'Score: 0' in white bold 24px font, id='score-display'.
- Top-right: 'Lives: 3' in white bold 24px font, id='lives-display'. Lives start at 3.
- Top-center: 'Difficulty: 1' in yellow bold 20px font, id='difficulty-display'.
- Center screen: 'Speed: 15.0' in white 16px font, id='speed-display'.
- A 'Start Game' button (id='start-button') centered on screen. Game begins paused; clicking this starts the game and hides the button.
- When lives reach 0, show a 'Game Over' overlay (id='gameover-overlay') with final score and a 'Restart' button (id='restart-button').

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- gameStarted: boolean
- gameOver: boolean
- score: number (integer)
- lives: number (0-3)
- difficultyLevel: number (1-10)
- currentSpeed: number (scroll speed)
- skierX: number (skier X position)
- elapsedTime: number (seconds since game start)
- fishCollected: number (total fish collected)
- isInvincible: boolean
- obstacleCount: number (active obstacles on screen)
- fishOnScreen: number (active fish on screen)
- skierExists: boolean (true if skier mesh exists in scene)
- frameCount: number (total frames since game start)
physics_constraints: Skier X clamped to [-18, 18]. Collision radius 1.5 for obstacles, 2.0 for fish. Speed = 15 + (difficultyLevel-1)*2. Difficulty increments every 10 seconds, capped at 10. Obstacle spawn interval = max(0.5, 1.5 - 0.1*(difficultyLevel-1)). Invincibility lasts 2 seconds after fish collection.
